input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign: vLLM ROCm serving parity and go/no-go scope

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: whether vLLM serving on AMD
Instinct accelerators achieves functional and performance parity with the
productized CUDA builds for the platform's supported model set. It runs a
validation campaign on physical AMD GPU hardware, records per-model functional
and performance results, and produces the go/no-go recommendation that
determines the scope of the ROCm serving runtime productization work.

## Scope

- Define the campaign plan for the supported model set: per-model functional
  checks and performance measurements (throughput and latency) against the CUDA
  baseline, on single- and multi-GPU serving configurations where applicable.
- Secure access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes (procurement or partner-lab
  access) — access itself is an externally-controlled precondition tracked as a
  risk, not a deliverable condition.
- Execute the campaign using upstream vLLM ROCm runtime builds on the supported
  model set.
- Record functional parity results (pass/fail per model) and performance parity
  data (per-model measurements versus CUDA baseline).
- Produce the go/no-go report: the per-model list cleared for productization,
  gaps found, and the recommended productization scope.
- Track upstream ROCm image availability for the models and configurations
  under test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation report exists covering every model in the supported model set,
  with functional pass/fail results and performance measurements recorded from
  execution on physical AMD Instinct hardware.
- Each model's functional result is a defined pass/fail against the CUDA
  baseline behavior for the same serving configuration.
- Performance data (throughput and latency) is captured per model and compared
  against the CUDA baseline in the report.
- The report states a per-model go/no-go recommendation and an overall
  recommended productization scope, such that the serving runtime
  productization work can proceed on a defined model list.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
  establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
  supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

## Risks / Notes

- Hardware access is unresolved (procurement or partner-lab); it is externally
  controlled and may gate campaign start timing.
- Upstream ROCm runtime image release cadence is controlled by AMD and the
  upstream communities; image availability for specific models or
  configurations may lag.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for campaign-cleared models

## Description

This epic delivers a supported, productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime image and
its serving runtime definition, covering the models cleared by the AMD Instinct
validation campaign. It turns the validated upstream ROCm capability into a
platform-shipped runtime that deploys under KServe InferenceServices alongside
the existing CUDA builds.

## Scope

- Build the vLLM ROCm runtime image variant from the upstream ROCm base images,
  through the existing runtime image build and release pipeline used for
  productized runtimes.
- Publish the ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime definition for the ROCm
  vLLM runtime so it can be selected for InferenceService deployment.
- Restrict the declared supported model list to the models cleared by the
  validation campaign's go/no-go report.
- Verify KServe compatibility: InferenceServices using the ROCm runtime deploy
  and reach Ready (including raw deployment mode, the recommended path for
  disconnected environments).
- Keep the existing CUDA (NVIDIA) vLLM builds unaffected — the ROCm runtime is
  additive, not a replacement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A vLLM ROCm runtime image builds and releases green through the existing
  runtime image pipeline, with the image published for the platform release.
- A ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime definition for the ROCm vLLM runtime
  is published and deployable.
- An InferenceService using the ROCm vLLM runtime for a cleared model deploys
  successfully and reaches Ready, including in raw deployment mode.
- The documented supported model list for the ROCm runtime matches exactly the
  models cleared by the validation campaign's go/no-go report.
- Existing CUDA vLLM runtime builds and their ServingRuntime definitions are
  unchanged by this work.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears.

## Risks / Notes

- Upstream ROCm runtime image release cadence is controlled by AMD and may not
  align with platform release trains; mitigation is pinning to validated image
  versions and rebuilding as needed.
- The epic's scope (which models are covered) is determined by the validation
  campaign outcome; if no model clears, this epic is removed and parity gaps
  are reported upstream instead.

# PyTorch ROCm training support for single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs

## Description

This epic enables PyTorch training on AMD Instinct accelerators using the
Training Operator: PyTorchJobs running ROCm PyTorch training images execute
correctly on AMD GPU nodes for both single-GPU and multi-GPU (including
multi-node) job topologies, admitted through Kueue workload queueing.

## Scope

- Enable and validate PyTorchJob execution with ROCm PyTorch training images
  on AMD Instinct worker nodes, for single-GPU and multi-GPU distributed
  topologies.
- Verify job specs request AMD GPU resources (amd.com/gpu) correctly for the
  job topology, including gang-scheduled multi-node jobs.
- Validate that PyTorchJobs requesting amd.com/gpu are admitted through Kueue
  queueing and run to completion (the quota configuration itself is delivered
  by the Kueue quota handling work; this epic validates training jobs against
  it as an acceptance gate).
- Document any Training Operator changes or configuration needed for ROCm
  worker nodes (driver/runtime prerequisites on the job pods).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob using a ROCm PyTorch training image runs to
  completion on an AMD Instinct node with correct training results.
- A multi-GPU (and multi-node, where topology permits) PyTorchJob using ROCm
  PyTorch training images runs to completion with distributed training
  functioning correctly across GPUs.
- PyTorchJobs requesting amd.com/gpu resources are admitted through Kueue
  queueing and execute on AMD GPU nodes.
- Any driver/runtime prerequisites for ROCm job pods are identified and
  recorded for inclusion in product documentation.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)** (partial): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single-
  and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue — the Training Operator / job
  execution portion. The amd.com/gpu quota handling portion is covered by the
  Kueue quota configuration work.

## Risks / Notes

- Requires access to AMD Instinct nodes for validation; shared with the
  serving validation campaign (coordination risk, not a dependency).
- Relies on upstream PyTorch ROCm image/wheel availability for the tested
  PyTorch versions.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for ROCm workloads

## Description

This epic delivers amd.com/gpu quota handling in the platform's Kueue-based
distributed workloads stack, so that workloads requesting AMD GPU resources are
admitted with correct quota accounting — queued when quota is exhausted,
admitted when capacity is available, with all-or-nothing gang semantics for
multi-pod jobs.

## Scope

- Define the Kueue resource flavor and ClusterQueue/LocalQueue configuration
  covering the amd.com/gpu resource, so AMD GPU capacity is quota-managed like
  existing accelerator resources.
- Implement or configure quota accounting for amd.com/gpu requests in
  workload admission (covering any code or configuration gap between Kueue's
  quota model and AMD GPU resource discovery on Instinct nodes).
- Validate admission behavior: workloads requesting amd.com/gpu are admitted
  when quota is available, held pending when quota is exhausted, and
  multi-pod workloads are admitted all-or-nothing.
- Deliver the quota configuration as deployable, documented manifests for
  clusters with AMD GPU nodes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A workload requesting amd.com/gpu is admitted through Kueue when quota is
  available and remains pending (not partially admitted) when quota is
  exhausted.
- Multi-pod workloads requesting amd.com/gpu are admitted with all-or-nothing
  semantics.
- Quota accounting for amd.com/gpu is correct: admitted usage counts against
  the configured ClusterQueue quota and is released when workloads finish.
- The quota configuration is delivered as versioned, deployable manifests with
  usage documentation.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)** (partial): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single-
  and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling —
  the Kueue quota/admission portion. The PyTorchJob execution portion is
  covered by the Training Operator ROCm training work.

## Risks / Notes

- Requires AMD Instinct nodes with AMD GPU resource discovery for end-to-end
  validation; shared with the other AMD validation work (coordination risk,
  not a dependency).

# Document AMD hardware support, driver prerequisites, and validated model list

## Description

This epic authors the product documentation for AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement:
which AMD hardware is supported, the driver and runtime prerequisites for
serving and training on AMD Instinct accelerators, and the list of models
validated for the ROCm serving runtime.

## Scope

- New documentation topics covering:
  - Supported AMD Instinct hardware for RHOAI serving and training.
  - Driver and runtime prerequisites for AMD GPU nodes (ROCm driver
    requirements for both vLLM serving and PyTorch training workloads).
  - The validated model list for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime, as cleared by
    the validation campaign and shipped in the productized runtime.
  - Configuring Kueue quota for amd.com/gpu resources on clusters with AMD
    GPU nodes.
  - Any AMD-specific limitations relative to the CUDA (NVIDIA) builds, drawn
    from the validation campaign's findings.
- Follow the Red Hat docs content process for authoring, building, and
  publishing these topics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the supported AMD hardware for serving and
  training.
- Published documentation states the driver and runtime prerequisites for AMD
  GPU nodes.
- Published documentation states the validated model list, matching exactly
  the models cleared by the validation campaign and supported by the
  productized ROCm serving runtime.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented serving
  runtime, training support, and quota configuration, with review sign-off
  recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver
  prerequisites, and the validated model list.

## Risks / Notes

- Content depends on the validation campaign results (validated model list)
  and the productized runtime's supported model list; authoring starts only
  after those are final.
- If the validation campaign clears no model, the serving model-list and ROCm
  serving-runtime documentation topics are dropped or rewritten; the hardware,
  driver, training, and Kueue quota documentation content is unaffected and
  proceeds regardless of the campaign outcome.
